exposure: Induction of labor at 37-38 weeks' gestation for large-for-gestational age babies
Expectant management (spontaneous birth at >=37 weeks and planned births at >=39 weeks)
outcome: Infant admission to special care nursery or neonatal intensive care
cohort: The study included term (37+ weeks), cephalic-presenting singleton pregnancies with a large-for-gestational age baby in New South Wales, Australia, from 2002-2006.
finding: Early term labor induction for large-for-gestational age babies was associated with reduced cesarean section rates but increased risks of neonatal morbidities and subsequent childhood hospital admissions and special needs.
mod_finding: Women undergoing early term labor induction were less likely to have a cesarean section compared to expectantly managed counterparts.
gest_age: 37-38 weeks' gestation (for induction group); 37+ weeks (for term pregnancies)
